purpose: Current assessment, kept SEPARATE from qaSnapshot.json so that reopening a case never rewrites what was observed on the day it was verified.

findings.headline: The presentation is fixed. The relevance behaviour is not.
findings.whatWasVerified: On 2026-10-06 the presentation was checked on the released builds and still holds: a search matching nothing says so, and loosely-related suggestions sit behind an explicit action rather than being presented as answers. That verification is accurate about what it checked, and is kept in the recorded snapshot unchanged.
findings.whatRemainsOpen: The system still returns its five nearest matches however unrelated they are. Nothing in it rejects a result for being too far away.
findings.evidence: Measured against the development website on 2026-11-10. Two nonsense searches each returned five suggestions, from different record types. Measuring the similarity scores showed that no single distance cutoff separates useful searches from nonsense ones - the closest useful search and the closest nonsense search are a ten-thousandth apart. A check against the words actually present in the archive does separate them cleanly, and that is the recommended fix.
findings.blockedBy: The fix changes which suggestions the archive offers, so it is a change in its own right with its own testing and review.
findings.whatWouldCloseIt: The recommended check built, released, and re-verified on the development website against the same searches.
